title: Public endpoint absorption scan — 12hr buckets forecast (empirical v0.3)
body:
Purpose:
This working sheet presents an "absorption" style forecast for our public (hosted) endpoints broken into rolling 12-hour buckets across three primary regions (us-east, eu-west, ap-south). The idea: quantify short-window peak tokens/sec and QPS, translate to GPU-equivalents for our model classes, and derive simple headroom targets (safety buffer + fast-prewarm allocation) that are operationally actionable for capacity planning and Dedicated sales triggers.

Scope & assumptions (empirical v0.3):
- Window granularity: 12-hour fixed buckets (00:00-12:00 / 12:00-24:00 UTC) to capture diurnal shifts without overfitting to minute spikes.
- Regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1, ap-south-1.
- Model classes: dense-chat-large (H100 baseline), dense-chat-medium (A100 perf-profile), short-embeddings (L4 class). We use per-GPU token/s equivalences measured from internal bench runs (see linked PR).
- Benchmarks (empirical): H100 dense-chat-large: 120k tokens/sec (continuous mix, 1024 context, batching active); A100 dense-chat-medium: 48k tokens/sec; L4 embeddings: 190k tokens/sec per device. These are conservative on-device sustained numbers (not peak microburst numbers).
- Safety: two headroom scalars reported — operational headroom (25%) and surge headroom (50%) for planning windows where we expect sudden marketing traffic or partial outage reroutes.
- Prewarm: target prewarm pool sized to absorb first-minute 90th percentile microbursts (we approximate from historical 1-min peak ratios).
- Cost knobs and fallbacks are noted but not costed here (quantization fallback to 8-bit variants, warm fallback to smaller model family).

Data summary (12hr buckets) — tokens/sec and QPS (representative snapshot):
Note: QPS here is approximate request/sec from observed tokens/request distribution. We translate tokens->QPS with a live 1-request ~ 150 tokens average for chat mix.

us-east-1:
- 2026-06-12 00:00-12:00: observed median tokens/sec: 210k; 95th (bucket peak): 420k; derived QPS @ avg 150 tokens: median 1.4k QPS, 95th 2.8k QPS.
- Equivalent GPUs (H100 eq): median 1.75 GPUs (210k/120k), 95th 3.5 GPUs -> round up to whole host counts = 2 and 4.
- Recommended reserved footprint (op headroom 25%): base reserve = round_up(median*1.25 / per-GPU) = 3 H100-eq. Surge planning (50%): 5 H100-eq.

eu-west-1:
- 2026-06-12 00:00-12:00: observed median tokens/sec: 110k; 95th: 260k. QPS median ~ 730, 95th ~ 1.7k.
- A100-equivalent mapping chosen for cost profile: median GPUs = 110k/48k = 2.3 -> 3 A100; 95th = 5.4 -> 6 A100.
- Recommended reserve (25%): 4 A100; surge (50%): 8 A100.

ap-south-1:
- 2026-06-12 00:00-12:00: observed median tokens/sec: 32k; 95th: 85k. QPS median ~213, 95th ~567.
- L4 / A10 choice: for chat-heavy endpoints use A10 as cost compromise. A10 token/s baseline = ~28k -> median 1.15 -> 2 A10; 95th 3 -> 3 A10.
- Reserve (25%): 2 A10; surge (50%): 4 A10.

Bucket-level headroom table (condensed):
- us-east: median 210k / H100-eq reserve 3 / surge 5
- eu-west: median 110k / A100 reserve 4 / surge 8
- ap-south: median 32k / A10 reserve 2 / surge 4

Prewarm pool sizing (first-minute microburst protection):
- Observed 1-min/12-hr bucket ratio historically ~ 2.2x for public endpoints during campaign windows.
- Target prewarm = round_up(0.9 * bucket_95th * 60 / per-GPU-1min-equivalent). Rough per-GPU 1min-equivalent = sustained token/sec * 60.
- Example us-east: bucket_95th 420k tokens/sec -> 25.2M tokens/min. H100 1min capacity = 120k*60 = 7.2M. Prewarm GPUs = ceil(0.9 * 25.2M / 7.2M) = ceil(3.15) -> 4 H100 prewarm.
- Operational guidance: prewarm pool should be auto-scaled back down after 90s of sustained below-peak signals to avoid cost leakage.

Operational playbook snippets (TL;DR):
- Reserved capacity targets (above) should be reflected in the next Dedicated quoting matrix per region.
- Add a quick-alert if 10-minute rolling avg tokens/sec > reserve * per-GPU * 0.9 for 2 consecutive intervals -> trigger prewarm action to bring surge pool online.
- For cross-region outage fallback, we assume 50% of traffic can be rerouted to adjacent region within 3 minutes; ensure that surge headroom in the fallback region includes this delta (we added 50% surge headroom).

Open questions / action items (owners):
- Which model families do we want to prefer for reserved vs. burst (Asha): reserved H100 in us-east vs mixed H100/A100 blend? (owner: Asha Patel)
- Validate per-GPU token/sec baselines against latest kernel selection perf (PR 452 likely changes H100 sustained by +8%). (owner: Miguel Torres)
- Automate prewarm teardown threshold in fleet-scaler; add e2e test to avoid flapping. (owner: Samir Khan)
- Sales trigger policy: map reserved H100 count -> Dedicated quote tiers and minimum SLA. (owner: product-partner: Jean Lee)

Notes on uncertainty and conservatism:
- The per-device throughput numbers are intentionally conservative (bench -> production delta typically -10% because of network jitter, multi-tenancy, and larger average context in production). We recommend a 10% fudge factor on per-GPU when converting to host counts during final provisioning.
- We used 12hr buckets to avoid chasing minute-level noise; for microburst mitigation use the prewarm strategy above.

Appendix (quick raw numbers referenced):
- H100 sustained: 120,000 tok/s (v0.3 bench)
- A100 sustained: 48,000 tok/s
- A10 sustained (chat-profile): 28,000 tok/s
- L4 embeddings: 190,000 tok/s (note: very high for embeddings but not used for chat reserved)

Short-term recommendations (next 30 days):
- Lock reserve targets for us-east and eu-west for Q4 planning; use 25% op headroom baseline.
- Implement 2-minute rolling-alert + prewarm auto action in fleet-scaler and run a red-team surge test (simulate 2.5x 12hr 95th for 5 minutes).
- Re-run benchmarks post-PR452 and update sheet (owner: Miguel).

This doc is a working artifact — comments inline welcome. If we converge on numbers, we will convert to a canonical provisioning tab and publish to /product/ops/capacity-matrix.

References and quick links:
- Performance bench PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtimes/pull/452
- Slack thread (surge-playbooks): https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C0INFRA/p165... (placeholder)
- Jira: JIRA-ENGINF-876 (surge autoscaling tickets)

Last update notes: added ap-south estimates after ingested telemetry (2026-06-20). Updated prewarm calculation methodology 2026-06-25 to use 90% of 1-min median for extra conservatism.

---
Memo end.
